title: Nearly Two Million Fans Line Madrid Streets as Spain’s World Cup Champions Come Home
excerpt: King Felipe, Queen Letizia, and Prime Minister Sánchez welcomed La Roja before an open-top bus parade through packed streets, as Ferran Torres wore a Make Spain Great Again cap.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Nearly two million fans celebrated Spain's World Cup victory in Madrid, surpassing the 2010 turnout.
  • Ferran Torres wore a 'Make Spain Great Again' cap during the victory parade.
  • King Felipe hailed the win as an epic triumph, while PM Sánchez hinted at a 2030 World Cup bid.
  • Nine players from Spain's squad are from FC Barcelona; no Real Madrid players were included.

> **"For the nearly two million who turned out — and the millions more watching from across the globe — it was a party 16 years in the making.

"**
  • Close to two million people flooded Madrid’s streets on Monday to celebrate Spain’s 1-0 World Cup final victory over Argentina
  • Match-winner Ferran Torres wore a Make Spain Great Again cap during the open-top bus parade to Plaza de Cibeles
  • King Felipe called it an epic triumph, while PM Sánchez floated the idea of a third World Cup in 2030 when Spain co-hosts
  • Nine of Spain’s squad play for FC Barcelona, with no Real Madrid player in the World Cup-winning team

Less than 24 hours after Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike sealed Spain’s second World Cup title, the champions landed at Madrid-Barajas Airport to scenes not seen in the Spanish capital since 2010.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ebSt0kmLiB0

Royal Welcome, Then the Streets

The celebrations followed a precise choreography. After touching down around midday on Monday, the squad headed to the Zarzuela Palace where King Felipe, Queen Letizia, and Princesses Leonor and Sofía were waiting. It has been an epic triumph, King Felipe told the squad, according to The Times. You’ve won with style. When Spain plays, we’re all in it.

From there, the team moved to the Moncloa Palace for a reception with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who couldn’t resist looking ahead. Why not assume that good things come in threes? he said, alluding to Spain’s 2030 World Cup hosting bid with Portugal and Morocco, according to Reuters.

A City Transformed

At 7 p.m. local time, the open-top double-decker bus — emblazoned with Kings of the World and two stars — began its slow crawl from Moncloa to the Plaza de Cibeles, where Real Madrid traditionally celebrates its own titles. The irony was not lost on fans: nine of Spain’s World Cup squad play for FC Barcelona, with only Marc Cucurella, who recently moved to Real Madrid, representing the capital’s club.

https://x.com/FIFAWorldCup/status/2078963624266133887

Close to two million people lined the route, according to government estimates cited by Reuters — a turnout that exceeded Spain’s 2010 celebration. Fans in red-and-gold jerseys spilled across every block, with forward Borja Iglesias manning a DJ set atop the bus as teammates threw footballs into the crowd.

"Everybody was crazy. It was a very good mood. People were very happy. There were no problems, just a lot of happiness."

— Daniel Gaona, a Spanish national who travelled from Estonia for the final

Torres’ Cheeky Statement

Torres, the hero of Sunday’s 1-0 victory at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, wore a red baseball cap bearing the slogan Make Spain Great Again — a tongue-in-cheek nod to the American political catchphrase that drew laughter and photographs throughout the parade, OneFootball reported.

Meanwhile, 18-year-old Lamine Yamal, widely tipped as the tournament’s breakout talent, sported a distinctive headpiece that became an instant social media sensation. The teenage Barcelona forward has now won a European Championship and a World Cup before turning 19.

2030 Already on the Horizon

Spain’s triumph adds momentum to the 2030 tournament, which Spain will co-host with Portugal and Morocco. Coach Luis de la Fuente struck a grateful tone at Moncloa. We have experienced this with the pride that comes from representing a wonderful country, he told Sánchez. They are, without a doubt, the best team in the world.

The celebrations at Plaza de Cibeles, which included live performances from Spanish artists, were expected to continue past midnight. For the nearly two million who turned out — and the millions more watching from across the globe — it was a party 16 years in the making.
